entries.test: Public technical disclosures and research available by March 6, 2024 would establish how much was known about GPT-4’s precise internal mechanisms and training data.
entries.note: The context makes this a claim about public knowledge.

entries.test: Public evidence about OpenAI’s use of creators’ protected works, permissions, commercial exploitation, and resulting benefits would test the allegation of effective intellectual-property appropriation for profit.
entries.note: “Effectively stealing” alleges concrete conduct, although it does not specify a legal finding of theft. “I would argue” signals an endorsed argument, not a probability.
The extracted claim judges the honesty of OpenAI’s characterization of its mission.

entries.test: The New Yorker’s meeting account and any public contemporaneous records would establish whether OpenAI representatives acknowledged the open-source misconception and instructed others to leave it uncorrected.
entries.note: The surrounding context supplies the meeting and misconception. The allegation of awareness is tied to a reported explicit instruction that public evidence could substantiate.
The proverb expresses distrust without committing to a specific testable outcome.

entries.test: The January examples and publicly documented outputs from Marcus’s March 6, 2024 experiment would show whether similarly apparent reproductions of protected material continued.
entries.note: “Apparent” preserves the distinction between observable resemblance and legally established infringement.
